source.title: Relative Representations of Latent Spaces enable Efficient Semantic Channel Equalization
source.authors: Tomás Hüttebräucker; S. Fiorellino; Mohamed Sana; P. Di Lorenzo; E. Strinati

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure labels and plotted values are garbled in the web text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether representations from independently trained encoders can be made usable across models through relative representations, but in a semantic-communication setting and with task accuracy and reconstruction error as outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own Tiny-ImageNet equalization results, which bear on V4. It does not test convergence with scale, vision-language alignment, convergence across seeds, recurring features, or the causes of partial alignment. Claims and results cited from prior work are not treated as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The paper maps one independently trained, ImageNet-pretrained encoder's latent space onto another's through relative representations and a pseudo-inverse. The encoders differ in architecture and pretraining objective (ViT-ResNet hybrid, CLIP ViT, EfficientNet). It then measures the receiver decoder's Tiny-ImageNet accuracy. That cross-model accuracy is the V4 quantity, measured in a new setting (semantic communication). The paper is not one of V4's original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress that a target model's weak encoder can be compensated for by a more powerful transmitter encoder. They say prototypical anchors 'significantly' enhance performance, while the results section says only 'almost all' experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Uses anchor-based relative representations but applies them to semantic channel equalization, with an optimization-based pseudo-inverse and a new prototypical-anchor selection method; evaluates classification accuracy and representation reconstruction error rather than a scale trend in representation alignment.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy changes with anchor count and anchor-selection method; the closed-form inverse loses performance at high anchor counts. The paper also notes that clustering choice and centroid estimation can affect prototypical-anchor performance.
record.problems: Evidence is limited to one image-classification dataset and a set of ImageNet-pretrained feature extractors. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Several plotted values and their exact model-pair assignments are not recoverable from the garbled figure text.
record.rows_left_out: Per-curve numeric results from Figures 2 and 3 were not extracted because the web text garbles the plotted labels and values, preventing reliable assignment to specific model pairs. The prose-level findings are recorded in r1-r5.

untested.parts: Linear maps, layer stitching and mapping without paired data are not tested. Only image classification on Tiny-ImageNet is used, with three ImageNet-pretrained encoders. No readable numeric loss relative to the matched encoder is given.
Cosine similarity and normalized distance are both used, but no explicit comparison of alignment across metrics is stated in prose.

missing.what: Per-pair accuracy of the equalized transmitter versus the matched-transmitter baseline, for each receiver, similarity function and anchor count. Without it the size of the cross-model loss cannot be judged.
Accuracy under cosine similarity versus normalized Euclidean distance as the relative-representation similarity function.

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper whose evaluation metric doubles as evidence on V4. The relative-representations framework (Moschella et al.) is assumed rather than tested anew. The study uses three encoders, reports no uncertainty, and its figure values are unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no test of whether alignment rises with scale.
No paired image-caption vision-language models or cross-modal alignment test.
No comparison of models trained from different seeds for shared features or subspaces.
Tests anchor-based relative-space equalization with a pseudo-inverse on a classification task; does not test linear maps, layer stitching, unpaired-data mapping, or other forms of interchangeability.
No test for recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Uses cosine similarity and normalized Euclidean distance, but does not report a clear result establishing that measured convergence changes with the similarity metric, its settings, or input distribution.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: Semantic channel equalization system (reported encoder/decoder pairs, aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: Feature extractors pretrained on ImageNet; classifiers trained on Tiny-ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate classification accuracy after relative-representation semantic equalization while varying the number of anchors.

conditions.value: varied; exact values not stated in prose

rows.value: Accuracy increases as the number of anchors increases.
rows.note: The trend is stated in the text; the plotted values are not reliably recoverable from the garbled figure text.
rows.check: The baseline should be the matched-encoder accuracy, not lower anchor counts. The text says equalization is 'clearly effective', and accuracy rises with the number of anchors.

rows.subject: Semantic channel equalization system (reported encoder/decoder pairs, aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: Feature extractors pretrained on ImageNet; classifiers trained on Tiny-ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compare equalization accuracy using prototypical anchors against random anchor selection.
rows.value: Prototypical anchors improve equalization performance in almost all experiments.
rows.note: The result is explicitly qualified as occurring in almost all, not all, experiments.
rows.check: This compares the authors' anchor-selection method with random selection. It is a comparison of the study's own method, not a measure of whether representations are interchangeable.

rows.subject: Semantic channel equalization system (reported encoder/decoder pairs, aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: Feature extractors pretrained on ImageNet; classifiers trained on Tiny-ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compare the proposed optimization-based relative inverse with the closed-form inverse.

conditions.value: closed-form inverse uses cosine-similarity-based relative representations

rows.value: The closed-form inverse has similar performance, but loses performance at high anchor counts.
rows.note: The paper attributes the high-anchor-count loss to instability of the matrix inverse.
rows.check: This compares the authors' inverse with the closed-form inverse of [12]. It is a method comparison and should not be linked to V4. The baseline is also inverted: the closed-form inverse is the comparator.

rows.subject: efficientnet_b0.ra_in1k
rows.stage_stated: ImageNet-pretrained feature extractor; classifier trained on Tiny-ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compare the receiver's accuracy with a matched encoder and with a more powerful equalized transmitter encoder.

conditions.value: more powerful encoder; exact pairing not stated in prose

rows.value: The receiver sometimes performs better with a powerful equalized encoder than with its matched encoder.
rows.note: The paper gives this as an example-dependent result, not a general outcome for all pairings.
rows.check: For this pairing the cross-model mapping does not merely lose little: it exceeds the matched encoder. The state should be observed for this pairing, with the scope limited to receiver efficientnet_b0. The transmitter is a stronger encoder (vit_base variants) shown only in the figure.

rows.subject: Semantic channel equalization system (reported encoder/decoder pairs, aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: Feature extractors pretrained on ImageNet; classifiers trained on Tiny-ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Relate target-representation reconstruction error to downstream accuracy after equalization.

conditions.value: accuracy as a function of reconstruction error

rows.measure: Classification accuracy and reconstruction error between the estimated and matched target representations
rows.value: The paper reports a clear correlation: lower reconstruction error generally accompanies higher accuracy, but lower error does not always yield higher accuracy.
rows.note: The text describes the relationship and its exceptions; plotted values are not reliably recoverable from the garbled figure text.
rows.check: The mapped representations are not reconstructed exactly (nonzero ||ẑγ − zγ||²), yet task accuracy is often retained. This bears on V4's 'little loss' only in the task sense. No numbers are readable.

relationships.condition: Relative-representation equalization between different ImageNet-pretrained encoders on Tiny-ImageNet, at sufficient anchor counts
relationships.reason: The text calls equalization clearly effective (r1). With receiver efficientnet_b0, a stronger transmitter encoder sometimes beats the matched encoder (r4).
relationships.display_finding: Equalization was effective, and stronger transmitter encoders sometimes outperformed the matched encoder with an efficientnet_b0 receiver.

relationships.condition: Low anchor counts, and exact recovery of the target representation
relationships.reason: Accuracy depends on the number of anchors (r1). The target latent is not reconstructed exactly, and reconstruction error correlates with accuracy only loosely (r5).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy depended on anchor number, target reconstruction remained inexact, and reconstruction error correlated only loosely with accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Relative-representation equalization on the tested Tiny-ImageNet classification task
reader_labels.reason: Equalization yields task accuracy, and accuracy improves with more anchors; the paper also reports that prototypical anchors improve results in almost all experiments (r1, r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across anchor counts, inverse methods, encoder pairings, and reconstruction-error outcomes in the tested task
reader_labels.reason: The prototype advantage is not universal, the closed-form inverse loses performance at high anchor counts, and lower reconstruction error does not always improve accuracy (r2, r3, r5).
